vignette: A 20-year-old motorcyclist has an arm that hangs at his side, rotated inward with the elbow straight, after a crash in which his shoulder hit the road. He can move his fingers normally. Sensation is reduced over the outer shoulder and forearm.
explanation: The waiter's tip posture with preserved hand function and lateral arm sensory loss is an upper brachial plexus (Erb) palsy from traction on C5–C6: shoulder abductors, external rotators, elbow flexors and supinator are lost.
